description: Checkout/conversion problem: conversion rate collapses for one day, dragging orders and revenue down with it.
Traffic spike (e.g. bot or referral traffic) with no proportional lift in orders -- traffic quality issue, not a real demand increase.
Sustained conversion rate drop over several days, e.g. a broken checkout step that wasn't fixed immediately.
Sudden refund spike, e.g. a faulty product batch or shipping issue.
Ad spend increases sharply for several days while revenue/orders grow only modestly: declining marketing efficiency.
Sustained traffic decline (e.g. site outage or search ranking drop) driving orders and revenue down with it.
One-day AOV spike, e.g. a bulk or premium purchase, lifting revenue without a change in order count.
Positive demand spike, e.g. a flash sale or viral moment: traffic, conversion, orders and revenue all jump together. A good anomaly, but still statistically unusual.
Sustained elevated refund rate over several days, e.g. a recurring product defect surfacing across many orders.
Broad sustained decline in revenue, orders, and conversion while traffic stays roughly stable -- points at a purchasing-behavior problem rather than a traffic problem.
